question.text: Ravi targets a retirement corpus of Rs.2,00,00,000 earning 12% p.a. (1% per month). If he invests at the beginning of each month for 30 years (age 30 to 60), his monthly saving is approximately:

explanation.text: The Logic: Using the annuity-due formula, PMT(1%, 360, 0, -2,00,00,000, 1) gives approximately Rs.5,665 per month when investments are made at the beginning of each month. Per NISM Series XVII (pp.22, 26-27), this PMT/FV approach is the workbook's method for retirement-corpus calculations. The Trap: Candidates often forget the timing flag (beginning vs end of period), which materially changes the required monthly saving. Using the end-of-period formula understates the contribution. Note: Delaying the start of saving sharply increases the required monthly amount — the cost of delay grows non-linearly. Use side-by-side calculations to motivate clients to begin early.
